title: 15.2% below poverty line, 2.8 mn affected
byline: Sri Lanka’s poverty profile, still benchmarked on the Department of Census and Statistics’ Household Income and Expenditure Survey 2006/07, shows that 15.2 percent of the population about 2.8 million people, lived below the national poverty line, highlighting deep regional and structural disparities that continue to shape development policy.

title: Israel hits Iran with new strikes despite Trump admonition
byline: Israel said it struck military targets in western and central Iran on Monday, even after U.S. President ​Donald Trump reportedly told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to refrain from further attacks.

title: Powerful earthquake hits Philippines, triggering tsunami alerts across Asia
byline: A powerful earthquake has struck the Philippines, destroying buildings and triggering tsunami alerts across Asia.

title: Iran suspends flights at Tehran international airport
byline: Tehran’s international airport suspends all incoming flights after Iranian missile strikes on Israel, local media says.

title: Oil prices rise following Israel’s attacks on Iran
byline: Oil prices have already started climbing, with the global benchmark Brent crude rising 3.63 percent to $96.75 a barrel in the hour after the strikes were reported.

title: Iran fires missiles at Israel after Beirut attack ‘crossed all red lines’
byline: Iran has launched a barrage of missiles towards Israel, after warnings from Tehran that Israel must halt its ongoing assault on southern Lebanon or face more attacks.

title: Death toll in Philippine quake rises to at least 15
byline: The death toll from a magnitude 7.8 earthquake in the southern Philippines has reached at least 15, with more than 100 people injured, disaster agency officials said.

title: Opposition protest over detention of Suresh Sallay
byline: A protest organised by several opposition political parties is currently underway near the Fort Railway Station in Colombo, condemning what participants describe as the inhumane and unjust treatment of former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay.

title: Vehicle imports remain steady despite surcharge: Customs
byline: Sri Lanka Customs says vehicle imports have not declined significantly despite the surcharge imposed earlier this year, with imports continuing to contribute substantially to state revenue.

title: Tamim Iqbal becomes new BCB president
byline: Former Bangladesh captain Tamim Iqbal has taken charge of the country’s cricket administration after being elected the new president of the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB), marking a significant new chapter in his association with the sport.

title: Red warning issued for strong winds and rough seas
byline: The Department of Meteorology has issued a Red Warning for strong winds and rough seas, urging naval and fishing communities to take immediate precautions as hazardous sea conditions are expected to persist until 10.30 a.m. on June 9.

title: PTA, ICCPR Act fostered culture of abuse and torture: Saliya Pieris
byline: Former President of the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) and first Chairman of the Office on Missing Persons Saliya Pieris, PC said that lawyers and human rights advocates had long condemned the abuse of laws such as the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) Act, and Emergency Regulations by successive governments.

title: AKD concentrates on quantity while Yahapalanaya on quality: UNP
byline: The United National Party ( UNP) yesterday questioned the accuracy of a recent report produced by a local think-tank comparing the number of pieces legislations approved during the time of the Maithripala Sirisena government with the time of Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s government in the first 18 months.

title: Crackdown on unregistered elders homes to begin
byline: The Ministry of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment said it will soon begin a crack down on unregistered elderly care homes while action will be taken against homes operating illegally without registration.

title: ‘Jean Aunty’ chased away from Suresh Sallay’s protest at Fort
byline: Jean Aunty, an Aragalaya activist, was chased away from the satyagraha held near the Fort Railway Station in Colombo against the detention of former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay.

title: Houthis say they’ll block Israeli sailing in Red Sea
byline: The Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen take responsibility for this morning’s missile attack on central Israel, as well as announcing that they will block “Israeli maritime navigation in the Red Sea.”

title: Vehicle owners to receive SMS alerts on number plates
byline: The printing of vehicle number plates, which had been suspended for more than a year, resumed today at the Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) premises in Werahera under the patronage of Deputy Minister of Transport and Highways Prasanna Gunasena.

title: Trump calls on Iran and Israel to stop ‘shooting immediately’
byline: US President Donald Trump has called on both Israel and Iran to stop attacking each other.

title: Kananathan pitches global investment vision to Kerala’s new Chief Minister
byline: Former diplomat Kananathan  held consultations with Kerala Chief Minister  VD Menon Satheesan, the veteran and senior politician who was elected as the Chief Minister two weeks ago, at the Chief Minister’s Office inThiruvananthapuram this  morning.

title: Kirsten revolution begins with Kamindu
byline: Gary Kirsten’s tenure as Sri Lanka head coach was off to a flying start when Kusal Mendis and Co. set up a comfortable victory over the West Indies in the opening ODI match last week.

title: Three Sri Lankans held hostage in Ethiopia rescued
byline: Three Sri Lankan nationals who had been held hostage by an organised criminal gang in Ethiopia have been rescued, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said.

title: China’s Xi Jinping arrives in North Korea for rare summit with Kim Jong Un
byline: Chinese leader Xi Jinping received a pomp-filled welcome as he arrived in North Korea Monday for his first visit to the secluded nation in seven years.

title: Sallay continues treatment at Colombo National Hospital
byline: Former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay, who was admitted to the Colombo National Hospital while being held in remand custody under a detention order, continues to receive treatment, according to hospital sources.

title: Dengue surge alarms authorities as cases jump by up to 40%
byline: Health authorities have raised concern over a sharp rise in dengue infections across the country, as confirmed cases this year climbed to 35,228, marking an increase of around 30% to 40% compared to the same period last year.

title: Ten dead after migrant boat capsizes near Malta, Italian coastguard says
byline: At least 10 people have died after a boat thought to be carrying migrants capsized near Malta, the Italian coast guard has said.

title: Death toll in Philippine quake rises to at least 15
byline: The death toll from a magnitude 7.8 earthquake in the southern Philippines has reached at least 15, with more than 100 people injured, disaster agency officials said.

title: National Water Polo Coach Resigns Over Selection Dispute
byline:
Sri Lanka National Water Polo Coach Thanura Abeywardena has resigned from his position, alleging political interference, disrespect towards the coaching staff, and a flawed player selection process ahead of the 2026 Asian Aquatics Championship.
In his resignation, Abeywardena claimed that the original national squad was selected following official trials conducted from May 15-17, with the top 18 players being named on May 20 without any objection

title: Over 70,000 premises inspected on first day of national dengue control drive
byline: More than 70,000 premises were inspected on the first day of the three-day special national dengue mosquito control programme launched by the Health and Mass Media Ministry.

title: A/L exam to begin on August 10; Grade 5 scholarship exam on August 9
byline: The Examinations Department has announced the dates for the 2026 General Certificate of Education (Advanced Level) Examination and the Grade 5 Scholarship Examination.

title: Women Parliamentarians review progress of probe into Anuradhapura child abuse case
byline: The Women Parliamentarians’ Caucus has instructed the relevant authorities to ensure that all ongoing investigations related to the case concerning the abuse of a girl in the Anuradhapura area are conducted strictly in accordance with court orders.

title: Three elephant corridors cleared to reduce human-elephant conflict
byline: The government has cleared three major elephant corridors that had been blocked for years as part of a national programme aimed at finding practical and sustainable solutions to the long-standing human-elephant conflict.

title: CSE slides sharply as Middle East tensions trigger broad-based selling
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) commenced the week under significant pressure, with both benchmark indices recording sharp losses as escalating tensions in the Middle East continued to dampen investor confidence. Concerns over the potential economic implications of a prolonged conflict, particularly on energy prices and Sri Lanka’s external sector, fueled a risk-off sentiment among market participants.

title: Judiciary will decide on Sallay: Fr. Cyril Gamini
byline: The Judiciary will decide the fate of former State Intelligence Service (SIS) chief Suresh Sallay, Director of Communications Fr. Cyril Gamini Fernando said today.

title: ’This is a sin even god will not forgive’: Suresh Sallay’s mother
byline: The mother of former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, Major General (Retd.) Suresh Sallay broke down in tears today as she addressed the ongoing Satyagraha opposite the Fort Railway Station, condemning what she described as the treatment meted out to her son and urging authorities to act with compassion.

title: Suresh Sallay still refuses food, now on saline: Wife
byline: Manori Sallay, the spouse of former State Intelligence Service Director Major General (Retd.) Suresh Sallay said that her husband was still refusing to take food at the hospital.

title: Police remove satyagraha tent against Sallay’s detention
byline: The Police today removed a makeshift hut set up by several opposition political parties that staged a satyagraha near the Fort Railway Station in Colombo this morning, condemning the inhumane and unjust treatment of former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay.

title: Ten injured in bus crash near Pinnaduwa Interchange on Southern Expressway
byline: About ten passengers were injured in a road accident that occurred near the Pinnaduwa entrance of the Southern Expressway in the Galle area this evening (08).

title: At least 32 dead after major earthquake strikes southern Philippines
byline: At least 32 people have died after a magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck off the coast of Mindanao island in the southern Philippines, officials say.
